globalRules: Mechanical evidence supplies leads, not meaning.
Inspect current source before making a semantic claim.
Disposition every issued lead exactly once.
Return one semantic item per proposed record; bundled records are invalid.
Discovery and semantic acceptance are separate acts.
Model agreement is evidence, not truth.
Earlier sweep artifacts are provisional and may be revised, split, rejected, or strengthened by later source-backed sweeps.
A retry narrows repair work when useful; exhausted or incomplete packets close unresolved and do not block later sweeps.

sweeps.name: Source-family discovery
sweeps.objective: Group implementation files into useful source families and identify their broad product area without cataloging every declaration.
instructions: Close every source-cluster lead.
Name an owner only when inspected source supports it.
Keep generated, vendor, fixture, and unsupported boundaries explicit.

sweeps.name: Reverse path coverage
sweeps.objective: Start from eligible paths and prove each cluster is represented, supporting, excluded, or an explicit gap.
instructions: Do not create one record per file.
Use bounded source inspection to connect paths to an existing family or propose one precise family.

sweeps.name: Capability and system discovery
sweeps.objective: Identify user-relevant capabilities and separately owned architecture systems rooted in each source family.
instructions: Distinguish a product capability from its implementation family.
Do not infer runtime reachability from declarations or filenames.

sweeps.name: Ownership and boundary adjudication
sweeps.objective: Challenge broad owners, shared-family boundaries, persistence owners, generated owners, and unresolved overlaps.
instructions: Countersearch for a competing owner.
Prefer an explicit gap over false consolidation.

sweeps.name: Parent-surface discovery
sweeps.objective: Find top-level, tab, route-entry, startup, and container surfaces before searching their children.
instructions: Treat mechanical mounts as starting hypotheses.
A parent may mount distinct children; a nested destination is not promoted to parent merely because it is visible.

sweeps.name: Meaningful interaction discovery
sweeps.objective: Map human-addressable controls and actions likely to appear in a request without indexing decorative labels.
instructions: Trace the action owner and visible effect.
Separate distinct commands even when they share one menu or toolbar.

sweeps.name: Surface and interaction adjudication
sweeps.objective: Verify mounts, owners, aliases, action boundaries, and parent-child relationships for mapped UI.
instructions: Use direct mount or destination evidence.
Do not accept a route because its label sounds right.

sweeps.name: User-journey discovery
sweeps.objective: Trace meaningful user journeys from entry through terminal outcome across surfaces and actions.
instructions: Record ordered transitions and decision points.
Stop at external or unresolved boundaries instead of inventing continuity.

sweeps.name: Data and item lifecycle discovery
sweeps.objective: Trace important documents, records, jobs, or items through creation, mutation, persistence, versioning, deletion, restore, and terminal states.
instructions: Identify the mutation and persistence owner at each transition.
Call out atomicity, compatibility, and recovery boundaries explicitly.

sweeps.name: Journey reconciliation
sweeps.objective: Verify that journey steps resolve to current surfaces, actions, state owners, persistence boundaries, and terminal outcomes.
instructions: Countersearch missing transitions and alternate exits.
Treat a same-agent earlier journey as a hypothesis, not acceptance.

sweeps.name: Child-surface discovery
sweeps.objective: Inspect each parent deeply enough to find all directly mounted child surfaces and their distinct entry actions.
instructions: Gate A: close every mechanical lead.
Gate B: decompose routed switches into one child per destination.
Gate C: perform a bounded omission search beyond supplied leads.
Gate D: reconcile children with existing records and return one record per distinct child.

sweeps.name: Child-surface adjudication
sweeps.objective: Validate discovered children against mechanical mount context and reject nested menus, decorative overlays, and bundled destinations.
instructions: Parent-mounted menus and blocking overlays may count.
Nested menus, loading indicators, and decorative overlays do not count without a separate human-addressable boundary.

sweeps.name: Targeted child omission search
sweeps.objective: Revisit only unresolved, bundled, duplicated, or mechanically suspicious child-surface boundaries.
instructions: Do not repeat accepted child discovery.
Resolve or preserve every remaining uncertainty explicitly.

sweeps.name: Behavior and state depth
sweeps.objective: Verify actions, reads, writes, state ownership, persistence, and externally visible effects for related semantic records.
instructions: Group records sharing an implementation neighborhood.
Separate objective source evidence from adjudicated semantic conclusions.

sweeps.name: Lifecycle and safety depth
sweeps.objective: Verify lifecycle transitions, approval gates, failure and recovery paths, compatibility boundaries, and transaction ownership.
instructions: Follow state transitions to their durable or terminal owner.
Do not infer safe replay, rollback, or atomicity from naming alone.

sweeps.name: Semantic companion and final reconciliation
sweeps.objective: Find missing paired owners and reconcile concepts, UI, journeys, implementation, persistence, verification, and explicit gaps.
instructions: Check reciprocal relationships and missing semantic companions.
Completion means every issued lead is dispositioned; it is not independent acceptance.
